column2: Euro Disney opened near Paris.
The Church of England voted to allow women priests.
The European single market came into effect.
Toni Morrison won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
The ferry MS Estonia sank in the Baltic Sea, killing 852 people.
Formula One champion Ayrton Senna died in a crash at the San Marino Grand Prix.
Cal Ripken Jr. broke Lou Gehrig's consecutive games record.
Austria, Finland and Sweden joined the European Union.
The first Pokémon games were released in Japan.
Garry Kasparov beat IBM's Deep Blue in their first chess match.
Comet Hale-Bopp lit up the night sky.
Tiger Woods won the Masters at age 21.
The International Space Station's first module was launched.
The final episode of Seinfeld aired.
A massive earthquake struck Taiwan, killing over 2,400 people.
Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace was released.
Israel withdrew its forces from southern Lebanon.
Scientists announced a first draft of the human genome.
The Human Genome Project published its draft results.
Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone was released as a film.
The first Spider-Man movie was a box office smash.
Former US President Jimmy Carter won the Nobel Peace Prize.
Finding Nemo was released in theaters.
The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King was released.
NASA's Spirit and Opportunity rovers landed on Mars.
Ronald Reagan died.
A deadly earthquake struck off Sumatra, Indonesia, months after the 2004 tsunami.
Live 8 benefit concerts were held around the world.
An earthquake struck Yogyakarta, Indonesia, killing over 5,000 people.
Montenegro became an independent country.
Al Gore and the UN climate panel won the Nobel Peace Prize.
Gordon Brown became Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
Fidel Castro stepped down as President of Cuba.
Spotify launched in Europe.
The Large Hadron Collider began colliding particles.
Somali pirates hijacked the cargo ship Maersk Alabama.
Floods covered a fifth of Pakistan.
A famine struck Somalia and the Horn of Africa.
Space Shuttle Atlantis made the final shuttle flight.
Queen Elizabeth II celebrated her Diamond Jubilee.
Facebook reached one billion users.
A train carrying oil exploded in Lac-Mégantic, Canada, killing 47 people.
Frozen was released in theaters.
A ferry carrying students sank off South Korea, killing over 300 people.
Scotland voted to remain part of the United Kingdom.
The United States and Cuba restored diplomatic relations.
NASA's New Horizons probe flew past Pluto.
A massive earthquake struck central Italy.
Fidel Castro died.
North Korea tested its first intercontinental ballistic missile.
Emmanuel Macron was elected President of France.
A wildfire near Athens, Greece killed over 100 people.
Black Panther became a worldwide box office hit.
Fires burned across the Amazon rainforest.
Boris Johnson became Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
The United Kingdom formally left the European Union.
Locust swarms devastated crops in East Africa.
NASA's Perseverance rover landed on Mars.
A deadly COVID-19 wave swept through India.
A volcanic eruption near Tonga sent tsunami waves across the Pacific.
Rishi Sunak became Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
Wildfires burned record areas across Canada.
The Wagner Group staged a short-lived mutiny in Russia.
Keir Starmer became Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
One Direction singer Liam Payne died.

Over the Top
going over the top in no man's land
The whistle blows. Your company climbs the trench ladders into no man's land as German machine guns open up.
Charge with your squad
You made it across and took the enemy trench.
Half your platoon fell in the wire, but you made it back.
Crawl from shell hole to shell hole
You crept forward slowly and survived the attack.
You were pinned in a shell hole until nightfall.
Stay low by the wire
The attack was called off before you had to go far.
An officer caught you hanging back.
a poison gas attack
Someone screams "GAS!" A yellow-green cloud is rolling over the parapet toward your trench.
Get your mask on fast
You pulled the mask on in seconds and breathed through the cloud.
You got a lungful before the mask sealed. You coughed for weeks.
Help a buddy with his mask
You got his mask on and saved his life.
You both swallowed some gas helping each other.
Run for higher ground
You scrambled out of the low trench where the gas pooled.
You ran straight into machine-gun fire.
a night trench raid
Your sergeant picks you for a night raid on the German lines to grab a prisoner. Faces blackened, knives and clubs only.
Lead the way through the wire
You slipped through the wire and dragged a prisoner back.
A flare went up and the raid turned into a firefight.
Cover the raiders from a shell hole
You held the flank and the raiders came back safe.
Your position was spotted and grenades came over.
Cut the wire and wait
You cut a clean gap and the raid went smoothly.
The wire twanged and the Germans opened fire.
an artillery barrage
The ground shakes for hours as enemy shells pound your sector. The dugout ceiling is raining dirt.
Sit it out in the deep dugout
The dugout held. You crawled out deafened but alive.
A shell buried the entrance and you dug for hours.
Man the firestep for the attack
When the shelling lifted you were ready, and the enemy attack was beaten back.
A shell landed in the next bay.
Write a letter home, just in case
You finished the letter. The barrage ended at dawn.
Your hands shook too much to write.
Sniper in the Ruins
Men in your trench keep getting hit when they peek over. There's a sniper in the shattered farmhouse ahead.
Use a periscope to find him
You spotted the glint and called artillery on the farmhouse.
He shot the periscope right out of your hands.
Raise a helmet on a stick as bait
He fired at the helmet and a marksman in your platoon got him.
You kept low until your unit rotated out.
Days of keeping low wore you down.
You've stood in freezing mud for two weeks. Your feet have gone numb and swollen.
Rub on whale oil and change your socks
Dry socks and whale oil saved your feet.
Report to the aid station
The medics treated you and you kept your toes.
The medic said you were lucky not to lose them.
Ignore it and keep going
You toughed it out somehow.
You could barely walk by the end of the month.
It's Christmas Eve. From the German trench comes singing, and someone holds up a small tree with candles.
Climb out and meet them
You traded cigarettes and buttons with German soldiers in no man's land.
An officer saw you and you were disciplined.
Sing back from your trench
Both sides sang carols all night. Nobody fired.
Someone on your side fired a shot and the singing stopped.
Stay on watch
You kept watch through the strangest, quietest night of the war.
You spent Christmas cold and alone on watch.
Rats the size of cats are eating the rations and crawling over sleeping men.
Organize a rat hunt
You and your mates killed dozens. Everyone slept better.
There were too many. They kept coming.
Hang your food from the roof
Your rations stayed safe.
They got it anyway.
You got used to them, like everyone does.
One bit you in your sleep.
enemy fire during a tank attack
Strange armored machines are clanking forward with your battalion. Your company is ordered to advance behind them.
Follow close behind the tank
The tank crushed the wire and you poured through the gap.
The tank broke down and drew every gun onto you.
Spread out in the open
You took the objective while the enemy shot at the tank.
You were caught in the open.
Ride on the tank's back
You rode right into the enemy trench.
You were thrown off when it lurched into a crater.
The man next to you hasn't spoken in days. He just stares and shakes. Then you notice your own hands won't stop trembling.
Tell the doctor
The doctor sent you back for a rest. It helped.
He called it cowardice and sent you back to the line.
Look after your friend
Taking care of him gave you something to hold on to.
Watching him got to you too.
You pushed it down and kept going.
It came back in nightmares for years.
machine-gun fire in Belleau Wood
Your unit is ordered to clear a forest full of German machine-gun nests. "Retreat? Hell, we just got here!"
Charge the machine guns
You overran the nest and the wood was taken.
The charge was cut down. You crawled back wounded.
Flank through the trees
You slipped around the side and silenced the gun.
You got lost in the smoke and trees.
Throw grenades from cover
Your grenades knocked out the nest.
They threw them back.
the Meuse-Argonne offensive
The biggest American offensive of the war has begun. Fog, forests and barbed wire stretch ahead for miles.
Push forward through the fog
Your unit pushed miles forward through the German lines.
The fog lifted and you were exposed.
Carry messages between units
You ran messages through the forest and kept the attack connected.
A shell landed near you on a run.
Hold the captured trench
The counterattack nearly overran you.
being cut off and surrounded
Your battalion pushed too far and is surrounded in a ravine. No food, little water, and your own artillery is falling short on you.
Send a carrier pigeon for help
The pigeon got through. Relief arrived days later.
The pigeon was shot down.
Try to break out
You fought your way back to your lines.
The breakout failed with heavy losses.
Dig in and hold
You held out for days until you were relieved.
Days without food took everything out of you.
A sack of letters arrives. There's one with your name on it.
News from home. You read it ten times.
Bad news from home. It was hard to keep going.
Save it for a quiet moment
You read it that night by candlelight.
It got soaked in the mud before you could read it.
Spanish Flu in the Camp
Men are falling sick by the hundreds. Fever, blue lips, and some die within a day.
Stay away from the sick
You kept apart and stayed healthy.
You caught it anyway and were bedridden for weeks.
Volunteer in the hospital tent
You nursed the sick and somehow never caught it.
You caught the flu yourself.
being strafed by an enemy plane
Two biplanes are twisting in a dogfight above your trench. One dives and opens fire on your line.
Fire your rifle at it
The plane trailed smoke and crashed behind the lines.
It came around for another pass.
Dive for the dugout
You made the dugout. The plane flew off.
You twisted your ankle diving in.
carrying wounded men under fire
Wounded men are crying out in no man's land. The stretcher bearers need volunteers.
Go out and bring them in
You carried three men back under fire.
You were hit on the way back.
Guide them with a rope from the trench
The rope helped men crawl back.
Only a few made it back.
You stayed in the trench. The cries stopped by morning.
The cries haunted you for years.
the last minutes of the war
Word comes that the war ends at 11 a.m. today. But your officer orders one last attack at 10 o'clock.
Go, but slowly
You advanced slowly. At 11 o'clock the guns went silent.
Men died in the last hour. You were nearly one of them.
Refuse the order
You refused and waited. At 11 the war was over.
You were put on report, but the war ended anyway.
a U-boat torpedo
Your convoy is crossing the Atlantic. A lookout shouts: a torpedo wake is heading for the ship.
Man the deck gun
Your gun crew forced the U-boat to dive and the torpedo missed.
The torpedo hit. You were thrown into the cold sea.
Drop depth charges
Depth charges drove the U-boat off.
The U-boat got away and struck again.
Brace and grab a lifejacket
The torpedo passed astern. Everyone breathed again.
The blast threw you across the deck.
Mine in the North Sea
a naval mine
Your ship is sweeping a channel in the North Sea. A spiked mine bobs up just off the bow.
Shoot it from a distance
The mine blew up harmlessly.
It went off closer than anyone expected.
Steer the ship around it
The helmsman eased past it.
There was a second mine you never saw.
Battle of Jutland
the battle of Jutland
The two great battle fleets have found each other in the North Sea. Shells as big as men are screaming overhead.
Keep passing shells to the turret
Your turret kept firing all afternoon.
A hit near the turret filled it with smoke and fire.
Flood the magazine before it explodes
You flooded the magazine and saved the ship.
The fire reached you before the water did.
Tend the wounded below
You kept a dozen men alive in the sick bay.
A shell burst through the deck above.
a winter storm at sea
Your ship is escorting a troop convoy across the Atlantic in a winter gale. The decks are coated in ice.
Chip the ice off the guns
You kept the guns clear the whole crossing.
A wave swept you across the icy deck.
Keep lookout for periscopes
You spotted a periscope and the U-boat was driven off.
You froze through the night and saw nothing.
storming Omaha Beach
The landing craft ramp drops. Machine guns rake the water. The beach ahead is covered in obstacles and bodies.
Run straight for the seawall
You made it to the seawall and up the bluffs.
You were hit in the surf but dragged to shore.
Take cover behind the obstacles
You were pinned down for hours.
Help the wounded in the water
You pulled three men from the surf.
The tide and the guns nearly took you under.
the Battle of the Bulge
German tanks burst out of the snowy Ardennes forest. Your unit is surrounded at a crossroads town, short on ammunition and winter clothes.
Hold the line
You held. Patton's tanks broke through to relieve you.
Frostbite and German attacks took a terrible toll.
Fight from the houses
You turned the town into a fortress.
A tank shell collapsed your building.
Scout for an escape route
You found a way through the woods.
You ran into a German patrol.
fighting in the Normandy hedgerows
Every field in Normandy is boxed in by thick hedgerows. Each one hides German machine guns.
Blow a hole with explosives
You blasted through and surprised them.
The blast drew fire from three directions.
Climb over the top
You went over and cleared the field.
You were silhouetted on top of the hedge.
Wait for a tank with a cutter
A tank with a hedge cutter punched through for you.
The tank never came.
the battle for Monte Cassino
The ancient monastery on the mountain looms over the valley. Your division has been ordered up the slopes again.
Climb the rubble at night
You reached the ridge under cover of darkness.
Flares lit you up halfway up the slope.
Carry supplies up the mountain
You hauled ammo and water up the goat paths.
Mortars caught your mule train.
a tank battle in the North African desert
Enemy panzers are rolling across the desert sand. Your anti-tank gun is dug in on the ridge.
Hold fire until they're close
You knocked out two tanks at point-blank range.
They spotted your gun first.
Your shots kept them at a distance.
Your shots bounced off their armor.
a night parachute drop
It's midnight over Normandy. The green light comes on. Flak is bursting all around the plane.
Jump and find your unit
You landed in a field and found your squad by clicking your cricket.
You landed far from the drop zone, alone.
Help the stuck jumper first
You freed his lines and you both jumped.
The plane was hit while you were helping.
Your squad has to clear a bombed-out town street by street, room by room.
Go through the walls, not the doors
You blew holes through the walls and surprised them.
A wall collapsed on your squad.
Throw a grenade in first
The grenade cleared the room.
It was a dud.
Cover the street from a window
You held the street while the others cleared.
A sniper had the same idea.
Your unit opens the gates of a prison camp. What you see inside will never leave you.
Share your rations
You gave everything you had. The survivors wept.
The food made some of them sick. You didn't know.
Help carry the sick to the medics
You carried people to the medics all day.
You caught typhus from the camp.
Write down what you saw
Your notes became evidence at the trials.
You couldn't bring yourself to finish.
jungle fighting on Guadalcanal
The jungle is hot, wet and full of enemy soldiers. Malaria is spreading through your unit.
Patrol into the jungle
Your patrol found and broke up an enemy attack.
Your patrol was ambushed in the vines.
Hold the perimeter at night
You held off a night attack on the airfield.
The night attack came straight at your foxhole.
Take your quinine and rest
You stayed healthy while others fell to malaria.
You caught malaria anyway.
the battle of Iwo Jima
The black volcanic sand makes it impossible to dig in. The island is honeycombed with hidden bunkers.
Clear the bunkers with a flamethrower crew
You cleared bunker after bunker.
A hidden gun opened up behind you.
Advance up the beach
You fought your way off the beach.
Mortars walked across the sand toward you.
Carry ammunition forward
You kept the front line supplied.
A shell landed among the ammo crates.
the battle of Okinawa
Rain, mud and caves. Every ridge on Okinawa is a fortress.
Assault the ridge
Your company took the ridge.
The ridge changed hands four times.
Clear the caves
You cleared the caves one by one.
A cave collapsed around you.
the fall of Bataan
Your unit is trapped on the Bataan peninsula. Food is gone, and surrender is coming.
Escape into the hills
You slipped away and joined the guerrillas.
You were captured on the death march.
Stay with your men
You kept your men together through captivity.
The death march was a nightmare you barely survived.
being shot down over Germany
You're a gunner on a B-17. German fighters and flak are filling the sky over the target.
Keep firing at the fighters
You shot down a fighter and the bomber made it home.
A fighter raked your position.
Help the wounded crewman
You kept him alive until landing.
Flak hit the plane while you were helping.
Bail out when the engine catches fire
You parachuted out and were hidden by the French Resistance.
You were captured and sent to a POW camp.
Prisoner of War
You've been captured and sent to a prison camp. The guards are watching, and some prisoners are digging a tunnel.
Join the escape tunnel
You crawled out under the wire and made it to a neutral country.
The tunnel was discovered. You got solitary.
Keep your head down until liberation
You survived on Red Cross parcels until liberation.
Hunger wore you to the bone.
freezing in a winter foxhole
It's ten below zero. Your boots are frozen to your feet, and the enemy is just beyond the trees.
Share body heat with your buddy
You kept each other alive through the night.
You both got frostbitten toes.
The fire saved your feet.
The smoke gave away your position.
Rescue a Downed Pilot
a rescue under fire
A pilot parachuted into the field between you and the enemy. He's waving for help.
Run out and get him
You dragged him back to safety.
Enemy fire raked the field.
Your fire let him crawl back himself.
He didn't make it.
crossing the Rhine under fire
Your boat pushes off into the Rhine at night. The far bank is lit by burning buildings.
Paddle hard
You made the far bank and dug in.
Your boat was holed and you swam for it.
Keep your rifle on the bank
You spotted and silenced a machine gun.
The boat next to you sank.
A letter arrives with your name in familiar handwriting.
Read it in your foxhole
Good news from home. You grinned for days.
A "Dear John" letter. It hit hard.
Write back right away
You wrote three pages by flashlight.
Your letter came back stamped by the censor, half blacked out.
Your squad enters an abandoned village. Doors, wine bottles and even a piano could be rigged.
Check every doorway carefully
You found and disarmed three traps.
You missed one.
You went around and lost a day.
The detour ran into a minefield.
being hit in a tank
You're commanding a Sherman tank. A Tiger tank is hiding somewhere in the woods ahead.
Flank around to hit its side
You hit its side armor and it brewed up.
Its gun turned toward you first.
Call in artillery
Artillery forced it to retreat.
The artillery missed and the Tiger fired.
Word arrives: Germany has surrendered. The war in Europe is over.
Celebrate with your unit
You celebrated all night with men who had become brothers.
You celebrated a little too hard.
Think of the friends you lost
You took a quiet moment for the ones who didn't make it.
The memories hit hard.
the attack on Pearl Harbor
Sunday morning. Japanese planes are diving on the fleet. Battleships are exploding all around the harbor.
Man an anti-aircraft gun
You shot down a plane and kept firing until it was over.
A bomb hit near your gun.
Pull men out of the burning water
You pulled sailors from the burning oil.
The fire spread across the water toward you.
Fight the fires
Your crew saved the ship from burning.
An explosion rocked the deck.
the battle of Midway
Japanese dive bombers are attacking your carrier. Your planes are attacking theirs. Everything depends on the next hour.
Load bombs on the flight deck
Your planes launched and sank enemy carriers.
A bomb hit the flight deck.
Fight fires below deck
You kept the fires from reaching the magazine.
Smoke filled the passageways.
a kamikaze attack
A Japanese plane is diving straight at your ship. It's not pulling up.
Keep firing until the last second
You shot it down just short of the ship.
It crashed into the ship.
It hit the water beside the ship.
The explosion threw you across the deck.
a U-boat attack on the convoy
Your convoy is crossing the North Atlantic at night. A tanker ahead explodes. U-boats are among you.
Hunt the U-boats with depth charges
Your depth charges sank a U-boat.
A torpedo struck your ship.
Rescue survivors from the tanker
You pulled dozens of sailors from the freezing water.
Your ship was a sitting duck while stopped.
going down with the ship
A torpedo slams into your ship. It's listing badly and the order comes: abandon ship.
Help others into the lifeboats
You got men into the boats before jumping.
You were trapped below as the ship rolled.
Jump and swim for it
You swam to a raft and were picked up the next day.
You spent days in the water with sharks circling.
a typhoon at sea
A typhoon is tearing through the fleet. Waves are higher than the bridge.
Secure the gear on deck
You lashed everything down and the ship survived.
A wave nearly washed you overboard.
Stay below and hold on
You rode out the storm below deck.
You were thrown against a bulkhead.
A German U-boat has sunk the passenger liner Lusitania. Nearly 1,200 people drowned, including 128 Americans. Everyone is talking about war.
Demand war
Hope for peace
America Declares War
Congress has declared war on Germany. Posters of Uncle Sam say "I Want YOU." Young men are lining up to enlist.
Cheer the news
Worry about the draft
Bond drives are everywhere. Movie stars are selling Liberty Bonds on street corners to pay for the war.
Buy a Liberty Bond
The government asks families to go meatless on Mondays and wheatless on Wednesdays to feed the troops.
Do your part
Eat what you like
Knitting for the Troops
Everyone is knitting socks, scarves and mittens for the soldiers freezing at the front.
Knit socks for the soldiers
Leave it to others
Every morning the newspaper prints long lists of the dead and wounded. People crowd around to read the names.
Read the lists
Stop reading the paper
The Spanish Flu
A terrible flu is sweeping the world. Schools, churches and theaters are closed, and people wear gauze masks in the street.
Wear a mask and stay home
Carry on as usual
At the eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month, the guns fell silent. The Great War is over! Church bells are ringing everywhere.
Celebrate in the streets
Remember the fallen
On the radio: Japan has attacked Pearl Harbor. America is at war. The stock market dropped the next morning.
Line up to enlist
Listen to the President on the radio
Every family has a ration book now. Sugar, coffee, meat, butter, gasoline and tires are all rationed.
Buy on the black market
Bond drives are everywhere. Movie stars are selling war bonds at rallies to pay for planes and tanks.
Buy a war bond
The government is asking everyone to plant a victory garden so farm food can go to the troops.
Plant one in the yard
No time for gardening
There's a scrap metal drive. Old pots, car parts and even fences are being melted down for tanks and ships.
Donate your old metal
Keep your things
The air-raid sirens wail. Every window must be blacked out tonight in case of enemy bombers.
Cover every window
Leave a lamp on
With the men away, war factories are hiring anyone who can work a rivet gun.
Take a factory job
Stay where you are
The radio says Allied troops have landed in Normandy. Churches are holding special services and everyone is praying.
Go to church and pray
Listen to the radio all night
Germany and then Japan have surrendered. The war is over! People are kissing strangers in the streets.
The guns have fallen silent. The war is over, and your country has lost. Soldiers are coming home hungry and bitter, and nobody knows what happens next.
Mourn the fallen
Be glad it's over
Your country has surrendered. The cities are in ruins and foreign soldiers are in the streets. The war is finally over.
Start rebuilding
The stock exchange closed for four months when the war began, the longest closure in its history.
War orders sent factory stocks soaring.
Stocks fell sharply as America entered the war.
Prices for food and goods have nearly doubled since the war began.
Markets are nervous about the war in Europe.
Stocks fell after Pearl Harbor.
Prices are frozen by the government and many goods are rationed.
With the war over, everyone expects a boom. House prices are climbing.

You were sent to a Civilian Public Service camp to fight forest fires and work on farms instead of fighting.
I refused to fight as a conscientious objector and was sent to prison.
refusing military service
I refused to fight as a conscientious objector and was given work at home.
You were assigned work on a farm instead of fighting. Some neighbors won't speak to you now.
I was caught dodging the draft.
I dodged the draft and lay low until the war was over.
You slipped away and avoided the draft. People whisper about you around town.

You were wounded and spent weeks in a field hospital.

Your ship is moored at Pearl Harbor on a quiet Sunday morning.
unit

You're heading for the trenches.
This is the real thing.

Say your goodbyes.

Your side lost, and the country is in ruins.
You earned the {1}.
The new GI Bill will pay for college and help you buy a house.
Will you stay in the service?
I was discharged and came home from {1}.

I decided to stay in the service after the war.

My {1}, {2}, was killed in action in {3}.
The Secretary of War desires me to express his deep regret

{1} that your {2}, {3}, was killed in action in {4}.
Collapse in grief

You can't afford a bond right now.

I caught the Spanish flu.
I caught the Spanish flu but pulled through.
You came down with the flu and lay in bed for weeks, but you pulled through.
I stayed healthy through the Spanish flu.
